turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on at, on and in for time?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: use at with clock times, on with days and dates, in with months and years.
Right: "The film starts at six o'clock." Wrong: "The film starts in six o'clock." Six o'clock is a clock time, and in is for months and years, so it is wrong here.
Let me think aloud with one example: "The zoo is closed on Saturday." I ask: what kind of time word is Saturday? It is a day. Days take on.
Now you try. Write in, on or at:
My train leaves ___ 5 o'clock.
